Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: roughly 210–240 BPM. key is minor. Black death metal.
Global Emotional Progression: Begin at maximum hostility and remain there. Verses, choruses and bridge should change through riff shape, vocal phrasing and cymbal pattern rather than through reduced intensity. Every section should feel like another stage of the same uncontrolled attack, with each new stage becoming more frantic and uncontrolled than the previous. The final section becomes even more frantic through denser blasting, harsher tremolo movement and increasingly desperate vocals before ending abruptly.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: An abandoned concrete environment, graffiti covered walls, late at night when its darkest, uncontrolled fires are the only source of light and heat as swarms of people dressed in dark clothing gather before the band on stage. The deafening amplifiers, sweat, feedback and a band performing with almost reckless physical intensity. Relentless, primitive, hostile and violent.
Sonics & Production Profile: Raw, abrasive and close. Guitars are sharp and grainy, bass is dirty but audible, drums are fast and physical, and the kick remains clearly perceptible beneath the blast beats. Avoid polished modern metal production, cinematic layers, orchestration, electronic elements and spacious atmospheric passages.
Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Singer A (Female), an extremely harsh female black-metal vocalist with piercing upper-register screams, torn rasps and occasional deeper throat-driven shrieks, the listener is unsure if she is singing or screaming during the more intense moments.
Vocal Style: From the start it is continuous extreme screaming with no clean singing, bracketed vocals sound like screaming whispering. Verses use frantic clipped phrases and savage sustained screams. Choruses become wider and more hysterical through doubled screams rather than melodic hooks. The bridge remains equally fast and violent, with prolonged desperate screams layered over uninterrupted blasting. The final passage should sound physically exhausted but increasingly ferocious.
Vocal FX: Minimal processing. Short dirty concrete room reverb, light saturation and occasional raw doubling. Keep the voice painfully close and human. During the most intense moments it may sound like the microphone is unable to keep up with the intensity of the singer.
Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: Tremolo-picked distorted guitars, distorted bass and full-speed acoustic drums enter almost immediately and remain active throughout. Do not remove the drums, guitars or bass for transitions.
Secondary: Non instrumentation sound, which may be the lead singer smashing a bottle, or kicking a box to accent a pivotal moment in the song
Groove & Foundation Progression: Maintain continuous high-speed double-kick and blast-beat propulsion across intro, verses, choruses, bridge and outro. Never drop into half-time. Never introduce a breakdown. Never reduce the pulse for dramatic contrast. Section changes come from alternating blast-beat patterns, snare emphasis, ride or crash changes, tremolo riff substitutions and short fills while preserving maximum forward momentum.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: Brief amplifier feedback and cymbal wash may mark transitions. Avoid solos, avoid clean guitar, avoid acoustic passages, avoid ambient interludes and avoid extended instrumental pauses. Finish with either an instantaneous full-band cutoff or a final violent chord struck directly out of the ongoing blast.

Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: bpm is 94. key is G, and scale is minor. Trap / Melodic Hip-Hop. 4/4 time, minor-key tonality. Dark, minimalist, sample-driven production with a heavy, deliberate head-nodding groove.
Global Emotional Progression: The track establishes a dark, brooding, and narrative-driven atmosphere from the outset, maintaining a consistent tension through the verses that mirrors a descent into depth. The emotional intensity remains steady but thickens during the hook sections, where the rhythmic density increases to simulate pressure, before resolving into a stark, cold conclusion that leaves a lingering sense of isolation. Ominous, paranoid, confrontational and emotionally cold. Sustained underlying tension, restrained hostility and quiet menace. Uncompromising confidence without triumph or emotional release.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: Urban street culture settings, underground cipher sessions, workout playlists requiring steady rhythm, or scenes depicting craftsmanship and determination in a gritty city environment. Desolate urban housing estates, dimly illuminated concrete stairwells, deserted streets after midnight, industrial decay, territorial confrontation and an atmosphere of constant threat.
Sonics & Production Profile: Raw, dusty, distinctly analogue 1990s hip-hop recording. Dark, heavily filtered low-midrange emphasis, gritty sample coloration, punchy drum transients, compressed dynamics and restrained high frequencies. Deliberately imperfect, claustrophobic and stripped of modern polish.
Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Two contrasting masculine voices, one deep, gravelly and resonant with a threatening nasal edge; the other slightly higher, thinner, rougher and more urgent.
Vocal Style: Hard-edged East Coast rap delivery, rhythmically intricate but conversational. Tight internal rhyming, clipped consonants, subtle syncopation, deliberate pauses and occasional phrases spilling across bar boundaries. Intimidating through composure rather than shouting. No melodic singing.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: Minimal vocal layering, occasional doubled phrase endings, short spoken interjections and brief unison responses. No sung harmonies or melodic backing vocals.
Vocal FX: Predominantly dry, forward and centre-positioned. Subtle saturation, compression and very limited room ambience. Natural roughness and breath detail preserved.
Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: A repetitive, haunting two-bar motif constructed from a heavily slowed, pitch-shifted acoustic piano sample. Its low, hollow, metallic resonance blurs the distinction between piano, bass and plucked string. Short, descending minor-key fragments repeat obsessively with almost no harmonic variation. Hard, sampled acoustic breakbeat drums provide the rhythmic foundation: thick rounded kick, sharp cracking snare, dry closed hi-hats and gritty ghost-note percussion.
Secondary: Subdued low-frequency bass reinforcement, faint dissonant sampled textures, distant eerie high-frequency tones and occasional background noise. Supporting elements remain buried beneath the central piano motif and drums.
Groove & Foundation Progression: Heavy, loping, midtempo boom-bap. Strong snare backbeats, subtly swung subdivisions, occasional syncopated kick placements and imperfect humanised timing. The repetitive instrumental loop remains almost unchanged, establishing a hypnotic, relentless momentum.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: Faint vinyl hiss, tape saturation, sample aliasing, subtle pitch instability, dusty high-frequency roll-off, hollow mechanical resonances and occasional unsettling background accents. Sparse and intentionally understated.

Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: Dark, gritty 1990s East Coast hardcore hip-hop, underground New York boom-bap, approximately 92 BPM, minor-key, raw street-rap aesthetic. Sparse, ominous, sample-driven production with haunting piano motifs, hard drums and subterranean bass. Structure

Sparse, atmospheric opening with isolated detuned piano notes and low-level vinyl noise. Gradual introduction of heavy drums and bass. The central piano motif remains recognisable and repetitive throughout, providing an unchanging sense of menace.

Verses maintain a stripped, spacious instrumental foundation, leaving room for dense, aggressive vocal phrasing. Hooks gain weight through thicker drums, doubled vocals and stronger bass emphasis rather than additional melody. Brief instrumental dropouts punctuate threatening statements. Final passages become increasingly oppressive before ending abruptly. Cold, confident and intimidating, never theatrical or comedic. The rapper sounds genuinely dangerous, calculating and territorially aggressive. Precise rhythmic emphasis, unpredictable pauses and sudden bursts of hostility. Sharp consonants and forceful syllabic attacks. Growls and guttural ad-libs should sound instinctive and animalistic rather than cartoonish. Preserve the natural imperfections of a raw, uncompromising street performance. Production Authentic mid-1990s underground East Coast hip-hop character. Dusty MPC-style drum sampling, gritty analogue saturation, slightly degraded piano samples, weighty mono-compatible bass and minimal processing. Punchy transients, dry vocals and thick, dark midrange.

Maintain an oppressive, claustrophobic atmosphere through repetition, unresolved harmony and negative space. Avoid modern trap percussion, rapid hi-hat rolls, glossy synthesizers, autotune, polished pop hooks, cinematic orchestral crescendos and excessive reverb. Overall sonic identity: A haunting, paranoid piano loop over brutally simple boom-bap drums, supporting a gravel-voiced, relentless street rapper. Cold, menacing, hypnotic and unmistakably underground.
Global Emotional Progression: Relentlessly threatening, paranoid, claustrophobic and cold-blooded. An atmosphere of constant danger, mistrust and impending violence. Controlled intimidation punctuated by explosive aggression. No emotional release, optimism or warmth.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: Deserted housing projects after midnight, flickering streetlights, wet concrete, shadowy alleyways, distant sirens, unseen threats, territorial confrontation and predatory surveillance. Cinematic urban dread, as though danger is waiting around every corner.
Sonics & Production Profile: Lo-fi analogue grit, dusty vinyl texture, dark midrange, heavy low-end, narrow stereo imaging and minimal harmonic movement. Repetitive, hypnotic arrangements emphasising tension over melody. Raw, oppressive and deliberately unsettling.
Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: Deep masculine baritone, gravelly, weathered, raspy and slightly hoarse. Heavy chest resonance, harsh consonants, dry throat texture and an intimidating low-register presence.
Vocal Style: Aggressive 1990s East Coast street rap. Menacing, conversational delivery with tightly controlled rhythmic phrasing, internal rhymes, syncopated syllables and deliberate pauses. Alternates between quiet, contemptuous threats and sudden explosive outbursts. Naturally rough, confrontational and unapologetically hostile. Occasional animalistic growls, snarls and guttural vocal punctuation. Absolutely no melodic singing.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: Sparse, rough male gang-vocal responses, aggressive shouted doubles, low-pitched echoes and occasional overlapping street-style ad-libs. Unison reinforcement of memorable phrases, never polished harmonies.
Vocal FX: Mostly dry, intimate and upfront. Light tape saturation, subtle compression, occasional short slapback delays on isolated words, gritty double-tracking and selective distorted emphasis. Minimal reverb.
Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: Haunting, repetitive minor-key piano sample forming the central musical identity. Short, dissonant, slightly detuned piano phrases with unsettling intervals, unresolved notes and deliberate empty spaces. Chopped, filtered and degraded as though sampled from an obscure, deteriorating record. Deep, ominous bass notes shadowing the piano's root movement. Hard, dry boom-bap drums with heavy, punchy kicks, cracking snares and dusty, loosely swung hi-hats.
Secondary: Faint atmospheric drones, occasional reversed piano tails, distant metallic resonance, barely audible vinyl crackle and subtle low-frequency rumble. Rare, eerie high-register piano accents. No lush orchestration, bright synths or cheerful melodic elements.
Groove & Foundation Progression: Heavy, head-nodding, approximately 92 BPM boom-bap rhythm. Hard snares on beats two and four, thick kicks with syncopated variations, restrained swung hi-hats and occasional ghost notes. Steady, repetitive, almost hypnotic groove. Bass remains deep, minimal and physically imposing. Short drum interruptions and sudden silences increase tension without disrupting the fundamental pulse.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: Subtle vinyl hiss, muffled urban ambience, distant sirens, ominous reverse swells, brief turntable scratches and abrupt tape-like cuts. Occasional piano notes left hanging in isolation. Selective silence creates a sense of unease and anticipation.

Global Metadata
Basic Attributes: Mid-1960s folk-pop torch ballad, around 72 BPM in E minor with a loose 4/4 pulse. One female voice and one fingerpicked steel-string acoustic guitar. A descending bass figure underpins a spare melody on the upper strings, with faint, slow tremolo on the notes that ring out.
Global Emotional Progression: The singer starts with the composure of someone telling an old story. Her voice grows more urgent as she reaches the hardest lines, then retreats into long pauses. The ending feels unresolved.
Application Scenarios & Imagery: An empty room after midnight. The singer sounds as though she’s telling the story to one person across the table.
Sonics & Production Profile: A narrow mono studio recording with softened highs, gentle tape saturation and a short, dark chamber reverb. Faint tape hiss comes through in the pauses, with a trace of pitch drift on the longest guitar notes. Keep the breaths, fret squeaks and pick attack audible.
Vocal Details
Vocal Gender & Timbre: A low, warm female mezzo with a smoky edge and clear diction. She sings close to the mic, just behind the guitar pulse. The first words of a line can sound almost spoken, with a little vibrato arriving late on held vowels. Let her voice grow fuller and more exposed when she rises in register, with a slight catch where the emotion breaks through.
Vocal Style: Sing the verses almost conversationally, letting the ends of lines fall away. In every [pre-chorus], climb into a fuller, urgent tone and hold the last stressed vowel until the voice begins to tremble. In every [bridge], follow the slower guitar pulse, sing just above a whisper and leave a breath between phrases.
Harmony/Backing Vocals: Keep the female lead solo and undoubled in every sung section.
Vocal FX: Keep the vocal close and centred in mono, with gentle tape compression. Let a short, dark chamber reverb catch the ends of held vowels. Keep breaths and consonants clear.
Arrangement
Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
Primary: One fingerpicked steel-string acoustic guitar carries the song. Open with the descending bass figure and let the upper strings answer the singer between lines. Pluck the bass notes more firmly in every [pre-chorus]. In every [bridge], slow down and reduce the pattern to soft, widely spaced single notes. Return to the opening figure in the outro.
Secondary: Use an occasional softly brushed two-note chord on the same guitar to mark the end of a verse phrase or the entrance to a chorus. Keep the [bridge] to single notes and room tone.
Groove & Foundation Progression: [intro]
Open with the descending guitar figure on its own. Let the high note ring before the vocal enters.

[verse]
Pick lightly under the voice. Play the upper-string melody in the gaps between lines, like a brief answer to each phrase.

[pre-chorus]
Make every pre-chorus an emotional peak. Hold the tempo steady as the guitar bass notes get firmer and the upper notes come closer together. Let the vocal climb and press into the words, then hold the last vowel with an audible tremble.

[chorus]
Return to the opening guitar figure. Let the voice settle into a simple, sustained melody and ease back after the pre-chorus.

[bridge]
Slow every bridge to around 58 BPM with loose, unhurried timing. Reduce the guitar to isolated soft plucks with long gaps. Bring the voice down to a near-whisper and let each phrase trail into silence. Resume the original pulse as the next section begins.

[outro]
Play the opening figure once more. Let the last chord decay until only the room tone and faint tape hiss remain.
Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: Give the sustained upper guitar notes a slow, shallow tremolo. Leave in a little fret squeak and finger noise. Let faint tape hiss emerge in the pauses, with a trace of pitch drift on the longest notes and a small mono room tail on the final chord.
